stories.headline: Nvidia invests $2B in Nebius to build 5GW+ of AI data center capacity by 2030

key_facts.fact: Nvidia will invest $2 billion in Amsterdam-based AI cloud company Nebius as part of a strategic partnership to develop hyperscale AI data centers
key_facts.excerpt: NVIDIA will invest $2 billion in Nebius, reflecting NVIDIA's confidence in Nebius's business and unique depth of engineering expertise across the full AI technology stack.

key_facts.fact: Nebius will deploy more than 5 gigawatts of Nvidia systems by end of 2030, equivalent to power needs of more than 4 million US households
key_facts.excerpt: The cloud firm would deploy more than 5 gigawatts of data center capacity by the end of 2030. This represents power equivalent to the needs of more than 4 million U.S. households.

key_facts.fact: Partnership spans AI factory design, inference and agentic AI optimization, and deployment of multiple Nvidia generations including Rubin platform, Vera CPUs, and BlueField storage
key_facts.excerpt: The partnership deepens Nebius and NVIDIA's relationship across the full AI technology stack, from AI factory architecture to production software.

key_facts.fact: Jensen Huang said AI is at 'another inflection point — agentic AI, driving incredible compute demand and accelerating infrastructure buildout'
key_facts.excerpt: AI is at another inflection point — agentic AI, driving incredible compute demand and accelerating infrastructure buildout.

key_facts.fact: Nebius shares jumped nearly 10% in premarket trading following the announcement
key_facts.excerpt: U.S.-listed shares of Amsterdam-based Nebius jumped nearly 10% in premarket trading.

stories.headline: Meta unveils four in-house MTIA chip generations, deploying new silicon every six months through 2027

key_facts.fact: Meta announced four new custom AI chips — MTIA 300, MTIA 400, MTIA 450, and MTIA 500 — to be deployed by end of 2027
key_facts.excerpt: Meta unveiled four custom, in-house chips tailored for artificial intelligence-related tasks... The MTIA 300 was deployed a few weeks ago, while the MTIA 400, MTIA 450 and MTIA 500 will follow, with a new chip released about every six months.

key_facts.fact: The MTIA 300 was already deployed a few weeks ago, with subsequent generations following at roughly six-month intervals
key_facts.excerpt: The MTIA 300 was deployed a few weeks ago, while the MTIA 400, MTIA 450 and MTIA 500 will follow, with a new chip released about every six months.

key_facts.fact: VP of Engineering Yee Jiun Song said the chips give Meta more diversity in its silicon supply and insulate against price changes
key_facts.excerpt: Vice President of Engineering Yee Jiun Song said the chips give Meta more diversity in its silicon supply and help insulate for price changes.

key_facts.fact: The chips are designed by Meta and manufactured by Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC)
key_facts.excerpt: Meta Vice President of Engineering Yee Jiun Song told CNBC that by designing custom chips, which are then manufactured by Taiwan Semiconductor, the social media company can squeeze more performance.

key_facts.fact: Meta will continue buying chips from other companies including Nvidia and AMD alongside its in-house silicon
key_facts.excerpt: Meta will continue buying chips from other companies as well.

stories.headline: Oracle names Cerebras as key AI chip supplier alongside Nvidia and AMD on earnings call

key_facts.fact: Oracle CEO Clay Magouyrk named Cerebras as an important AI hardware maker alongside Nvidia and AMD during Oracle's quarterly earnings call on Tuesday
key_facts.excerpt: On Oracle's earnings call, CEO Clay Magouyrk named Cerebras as an important maker of artificial intelligence hardware, alongside Nvidia and AMD.

key_facts.fact: Magouyrk said Oracle's infrastructure includes Cerebras chips and emerging designs from Positron, alongside Nvidia and AMD GPUs
key_facts.excerpt: We continually offer the latest in accelerators, from the most recent Nvidia and AMD options to emerging designs from companies like Cerebras and Positron.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI has started relying on Cerebras chips for a generative AI model for software development
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI has started relying on Cerebras chips for a generative artificial intelligence model for software development.

key_facts.fact: Cerebras withdrew its IPO filing in October 2024 and raised $1.1 billion at an $8.1 billion valuation, still intends to go public
key_facts.excerpt: The company filed paperwork for an IPO in 2024 but withdrew the filing last October. Days later, it announced a $1.1 billion funding round at a valuation of $8.1 billion, and CEO Andrew Feldman said Cerebras still intends to go public.

key_facts.fact: In the first half of 2024, Middle Eastern client G42 accounted for 87% of Cerebras' revenue, making client diversification critical
key_facts.excerpt: G42, backed by Microsoft, is headquartered in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, and in the first half of 2024, it accounted for 87% of Cerebras' revenue.

stories.headline: Macron says France's nuclear exports can power AI data centers at World Nuclear Energy Summit

key_facts.fact: Macron said France exported 90 terawatt-hours of decarbonized electricity last year and can leverage nuclear power to build AI computing capacity
key_facts.excerpt: In France, last year, we exported 90 terawatt-hours of decarbonized electricity. Thanks to our nuclear plants, we have the ability to open data centers, to build computing capacity, to be at the heart of the artificial intelligence challenge.

key_facts.fact: Macron made the remarks in his keynote speech at the World Nuclear Energy Summit in Paris on March 10
key_facts.excerpt: Macron said in his keynote speech at the World Nuclear Energy summit in Paris.

key_facts.fact: The summit was co-hosted with IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi
key_facts.excerpt: French President Emmanuel Macron and Rafael Grossi, Director General of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) attend the IAEA Nuclear Energy Summit in Paris.

stories.headline: UK council votes on 1GW Elsham data center campus that would emit 1M tonnes of CO2 per year

key_facts.fact: North Lincolnshire councillors are set to vote on March 11 on the Elsham Tech Park, a 1GW data center campus with peak annual Scope 2 emissions of 1,004,478 tonnes CO2 equivalent by 2033-34
key_facts.excerpt: North Lincolnshire councillors are set to vote tomorrow [Wednesday 11 March] on plans for a data centre which will cause one million tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions in a year.

key_facts.fact: The council report recommends 'minded to approve' and assessed the emissions as 'not significant' by comparing one facility against the entirety of UK carbon budgets
key_facts.excerpt: A council report, which recommends that councillors should be 'minded to approve' the planning application, states that 'peak annual Scope 2 emissions' caused by the data centre will reach 1,004,478 tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO2e) in the year 2033-34.

key_facts.fact: Tech justice nonprofit Foxglove accused the council of comparing one year of data center emissions against five years of UK totals, calling the methodology 'both mistaken and deeply misleading'
key_facts.excerpt: Foxglove has described as 'both mistaken and deeply misleading.' The council allegedly compared 'one year of the data centre's emissions against five years of the UK's total emissions.'

key_facts.fact: The campus would span 1.5 million sqm with 15 data halls, construction costs between £5.5-9 billion over a 10-year build, creating 650-1,000 full-time jobs
key_facts.excerpt: The campus would span 1.5 million sqm (16.1 million sq ft), making it one of the largest in the UK. It will feature 15 data halls with a combined power draw of 1GW.

key_facts.fact: The 1 million tonnes CO2 figure is almost equivalent to the total climate pollution from all UK domestic flights at 1.2 million tCO2e
key_facts.excerpt: The figure, which is almost equivalent to the total climate pollution caused by all of the UK's domestic flights (1.2m tCO2e), has been described in a council report as 'not significant'.

sources.title: Vote due on plan for data centre with one million tonnes of climate emissions

stories.headline: Robinson Helicopter launches Robinson Unmanned division covering Group 1-4 autonomous drones

key_facts.excerpt: Robinson Helicopter today announced a new company branch dubbed Robinson Unmanned, where the helo company will partner with subsidiary Ascent AeroSystems to provide what it called a 'full suite' of remotely piloted and autonomous drones.

key_facts.fact: The division will provide Group 1 through Group 4 drones via partnerships with Rotor Technologies and Sikorsky for autonomy capabilities on larger platforms
key_facts.excerpt: Robinson Unmanned will provide Group 1 through Group 4 drones, excluding only the largest Group 5 category.

key_facts.fact: Sikorsky will integrate its MATRIX autonomy suite into the R66 TurbineTruck for contested logistics missions
key_facts.excerpt: Collaborating with Sikorsky to integrate the MATRIX autonomy suite into the R66 Turbinetruck.

key_facts.fact: Ascent AeroSystems is ranked 10th on the Pentagon's Drone Dominance program leaderboard with expected $150 million in orders
key_facts.excerpt: Ascent participates in Pentagon's Drone Dominance program (currently ranked 10th on leaderboard).

key_facts.fact: CEO David Smith said 'This will be the next 100 years, probably, of business for us in parallel to our helicopters'
key_facts.excerpt: This will be the next 100 years, probably, of business for us in parallel to our helicopters.

key_facts.fact: Paul Fermo, current president of Ascent AeroSystems, will lead the Robinson Unmanned business unit
key_facts.excerpt: Paul Fermo, current president of Ascent AeroSystems will lead the Robinson Unmanned business unit as president.

stories.headline: NASA's 1,323-pound Van Allen Probe A makes uncontrolled reentry 8 years ahead of schedule

key_facts.fact: NASA's Van Allen Probe A, weighing 1,323 pounds, was expected to reenter Earth's atmosphere around 7:45 PM ET on Tuesday March 10, plus or minus 24 hours
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. Space Force predicts that the satellite will re-enter Earth's atmosphere on Tuesday at approximately 7:45 p.m. ET, plus or minus 24 hours.

key_facts.fact: The probe was launched in August 2012 for a two-year mission studying Earth's Van Allen radiation belts but operated until 2019 when fuel ran out
key_facts.excerpt: The spacecraft, Van Allen Probe A, was one of two satellites launched in August 2012 to gather data on Earth's permanent radiation belts.

key_facts.fact: Originally projected to reenter in 2034, unexpectedly active solar activity during Solar Cycle 25 caused atmospheric drag that pulled the satellite down 8 years early
key_facts.excerpt: Analysis at the time indicated they would re-enter the atmosphere in 2034; however, an unexpectedly active period for the sun caused atmospheric drag that pulled them closer, sooner.

key_facts.fact: NASA estimated the risk of debris harming a person at approximately 1 in 4,200, higher than some past reentry events
key_facts.excerpt: The risk of harm coming to anyone on Earth is low — approximately 1 in 4,200.

key_facts.fact: Van Allen Probe B, the twin spacecraft, is not expected to reenter before 2030
key_facts.excerpt: Van Allen Probe B isn't expected to re-enter Earth's atmosphere before 2030.

sources.title: NASA's Van Allen Probe A set to reenter Earth Tuesday

stories.headline: NHTSA opens public comment on Zoox petition to deploy 2,500 steering-wheel-free robotaxis

key_facts.fact: NHTSA announced on March 11 the opening of a public comment portal to evaluate Zoox's petition to exempt up to 2,500 purpose-built robotaxis from certain safety standards
key_facts.excerpt: Amazon.com Inc. subsidiary Zoox petitioned the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration in August for such exemptions so it could place up to 2,500 self-driving robotaxis across a handful of U.S. cities.

key_facts.fact: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said if approved this would enable 'the nation's first-ever commercial deployment of a purpose-built, steering-wheel-free robotaxi'
key_facts.excerpt: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy noted that, if approved, the exemptions would enable 'the nation's first-ever commercial deployment of a purpose-built, steering-wheel-free robotaxi.'

key_facts.fact: NHTSA Administrator John Morrison said 'We don't take this request lightly, which is why we want to hear from the public'
key_facts.excerpt: NHTSA Administrator John Morrison emphasized: 'We don't take this request lightly, which is why we want to hear from the public to inform how we should evaluate this.'

key_facts.fact: Only Nuro previously received a similar exemption in 2020; Ford and GM sought partial exemptions under Biden but received no final decisions
key_facts.excerpt: Ford and GM sought partial exemptions during the Biden administration but received no final decisions; only Nuro received an exemption in 2020.

sources.title: NHTSA takes 'milestone' step toward robotaxi commercial deployment

stories.headline: Xpeng launches VLA 2.0 autonomous driving test drives across 732 stores in China

key_facts.fact: Xpeng began nationwide test drives for its second-generation VLA 2.0 autonomous driving system on March 11 across 732 stores in China
key_facts.excerpt: The test drives will officially launch on March 11 across Xpeng's 732 stores in China, covering models including the all-new P7 Ultra, G7 Ultra, and X9 Ultra.

key_facts.fact: VLA 2.0 uses an end-to-end vision-to-action architecture and claims 23% overall driving efficiency improvement, up to 76% on narrow roads
key_facts.excerpt: VLA 2.0 uses an end-to-end vision-to-action architecture.

key_facts.fact: Deutsche Bank analysts call VLA 2.0 the key catalyst for Xpeng's sales recovery in 2026 after deliveries fell 42% year-on-year in the first two months
key_facts.excerpt: Deutsche Bank analysts believe the performance enhancements of VLA 2.0 will be the primary driver of Xpeng's sales recovery in 2026... sales volume in the first two months down 42% year-on-year.

key_facts.fact: Volkswagen is set to be the first external customer to adopt VLA 2.0, with global deliveries planned for 2027
key_facts.excerpt: XPENG's second-generation Vision-Language-Action autonomous driving system (VLA 2.0) will begin global delivery in 2027, with Volkswagen designated as the inaugural launch partner.

key_facts.fact: CEO He Xiaopeng called VLA 2.0 the 'DeepSeek moment for autonomous driving' and predicted full self-driving arriving within 1-3 years
key_facts.excerpt: He Xiaopeng hailed it as the 'DeepSeek moment for autonomous driving,' predicting the era of full self-driving will arrive within the next one to three years.
